name: Turbo Hearts
description: Turbo Hearts is an American Hearts variant introduced at Upenn in the 1980s by Richard Garfield, based on the Chinese game Gong Zhu. Four players receive 13 cards each, pass three in rotation, then may turbo-charge one of four special cards (Ace of Hearts, Queen of Spades, Jack of Diamonds, Ten of Clubs) to multiply its effect. Lowest score when someone reaches 100 wins.

content.text: Turbo Hearts is an American Hearts variant introduced at Upenn in the 1980s by Richard Garfield, based on the Chinese game Gong Zhu. Four players receive 13 cards each, pass three in rotation, then may turbo-charge one of four special cards (Ace of Hearts, Queen of Spades, Jack of Diamonds, Ten of Clubs) to multiply its effect. Lowest score when someone reaches 100 wins.

Turbo Hearts was introduced at the University of Pennsylvania in the 1980s by Richard Garfield (later creator of Magic: The Gathering). It is an American variant of the Hearts family and an American version of the Chinese game Gong Zhu (Catch the Pig). The parent game Hearts emerged in the United States in the 1880s and descends from earlier trick-avoidance games such as Reversis.

All 52 cards dealt one at a time clockwise; each player receives 13. After the deal, each player passes three cards face-down in a rotating cycle: first hand pass left, second hand pass right, third hand pass across, fourth hand no pass, then repeat.
